album.title: Radif of Persian Music on Setar I

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on C3 and dwells most on F in Hejaz. Avaz Abu'ata (0:44.3) introduces Eb, F, centred on F. The line peaks at F4 (362.4 Hz) at 1:03.0. It closes on the tonic (Eb4 → Dk4 → C4 → Eb4 → F4 → C4).

theory_fit.name: 12-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Reference only: distance from the semitone grid.

theory_fit.name: Vaziri 24-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Quarter-tone grid (koron/sori = exactly 50 ¢ from the natural note).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic C set in the catalog (Shur's finalis C (271.1 Hz), which Abu-Ata keeps (Farhat 1990, p. 35): the suite is one Shur scale from it (0, 137, 295, 499, 705, 995 cents) and three of its seven tracks voted it. The vote picked the 4th above, Abu-Ata's shahed (same page). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 180.4 Hz (F)
